The federal court will likely grant the remand motion, because only a defendant can remove under 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a), and this plaintiff is the party who removed the case, so the federal claims do not save the removal. The attorney's wish to avoid the judge is irrelevant to validity, but the court may also order the plaintiff's counsel to pay the employer's fees and costs under § 1447(c) because the removal lacked an objectively reasonable basis. The case goes back to the state court where the judge is assigned.

CONFIDENCE: 90
